transcript.text: Dropped a cast iron pan on my ceramic hob and there's a crack right across the front left ring. It still heats up. Can I keep using it until I get a new one?

No — stop using the hob now, including the uncracked zones, and isolate it at the cooker switch or unplug it if accessible. A crack through a ceramic hob can let spills or cleaning moisture reach live electrical parts underneath, creating a shock or short-circuit/fire risk. The likely issue is impact damage to the ceramic/glass top rather than the heating element itself. Do not pour water on it, clean across the crack with liquid, or place pans over it. Keep the area dry and avoid touching the cracked section while it is warm. It needs assessment for replacement of the glass top or, commonly, the complete hob. An appliance engineer or the manufacturer can advise what is available once the make and model are known.

Ok, understood. It's a Hotpoint but I can't get to the model label as the oven is built in underneath. Some pasta water spilled earlier and might have gone into the crack, and there's a red cooker switch on the wall, so I can turn it off there. What should I do next?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Turn the red cooker switch off now, then isolate the hob circuit at the consumer unit/fuse box if you can identify it safely. Leave it isolated and do not use any zone again until a qualified appliance engineer has inspected it. The most likely damage is the cracked ceramic/glass top from the impact. Because pasta water may have entered the crack, there is also a possibility of moisture underneath the surface, so this is no longer just a cosmetic break. Do not try to dry the crack with a hairdryer, lift the hob, or remove the oven to reach the label; an engineer needs to check the underside and electrical connections as well as assess whether the hob can be repaired or needs replacing. Avoid touching any plug or socket if there is any dampness nearby. When arranging the visit, tell them it is a Hotpoint ceramic hob with an impact crack and that liquid may have entered it. The model can often be found later in the instruction booklet, purchase paperwork, or on the hob once it is safely removed by the engineer.

plan: They asked: "Can I keep using it until I get a new one?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "crack across the front left ring after a cast iron pan was dropped on it". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
